# Fuel pressure regulator replacement under intake plenum

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Drain coolant and remove the upper intake plenum to replace the fuel pressure regulator. [t2016]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Drain the engine coolant to prevent overflow.
2. Remove the upper intake plenum to access the regulator located underneath it.
3. Replace the fuel pressure regulator, noting its position just right of the last intake port.
4. [Partial] Reinstall the intake plenum securely.

_Procedure reported by [t2016]._

## Parts

- #6 Spark Plug: Often fouled by extra fuel dumped from a leaking regulator diaphragm [t2016]
- Fuel Pressure Regulator: Located under upper intake plenum, bolted to fuel rail [t2016]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Check the vacuum line connection on the FPR for fuel presence to confirm a hole in the diaphragm before buying parts. [t2016]
- Drive the vehicle for at least 15 minutes after installation to allow the computer to relearn and adjust idle conditions. [t2016]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Replacing the regulator without first checking if it is actually faulty by inspecting the vacuum line. [t2016]
- Not driving long enough post-replacement, causing the ECU to misinterpret initial rich running conditions as a problem. [t2016]
